chunks: And by this chain of narration — from Muhammad b. Ya'qub, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Muhammad b. Sinan, from al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar — he said: and narrated to us 'Abd Allah b. 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hariz, from Muhammad b. Muslim, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) —

He said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not incense the shrouds, and do not anoint your deceased with perfume except camphor, for the deceased is in the status of one in a state of ihram.'

key_terms.الْأَكْفَانَ: the funeral shrouds (plural of kafan — the winding cloth)
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor — the sole fragrance permissible for use on the deceased
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: the muhrim — one in the consecrated state of ihram for Hajj or 'Umra
key_terms.تُجَمِّرُوا: to perfume/incense with bukhur (burning incense); Form II of j-m-r

ai.seo_question: According to Shia hadith, is it permissible to use perfume or incense on the funeral shroud of a deceased Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling attributed to Imam 'Ali (Amir al-Mu'minin, peace be upon him), as reported by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him): it is prohibited to incense the funeral shroud with bukhur (incense smoke), and prohibited to anoint the deceased with any perfume other than camphor. The jurisprudential rationale offered is that the deceased occupies the same legal status as a muhrim — one consecrated in the state of ihram for Hajj — for whom perfume is categorically forbidden.
